why: Every process goes to server A or server B, so the difference is total - 2 * (load of A). Minimising it is the subset-sum / 0-1 knapsack question: which subset sums are reachable, and which is closest to total / 2.
hints: If server A gets load S, server B gets total - S. Write the difference in terms of S only.
You need the set of all reachable subset sums S; then the answer is the minimum of |total - 2S|. That is 0/1 knapsack (each process taken or not).
Use a boolean DP over sums, or a Python big integer as a bitset: bits |= bits << load. O(n * total / wordsize) time.
pitfalls: A greedy 'give the next load to the lighter server' fails, e.g. on [3,3,2,2,2].
Either server may be empty; S = 0 is reachable.
If negative loads could appear, shift the bitset by the sum of negatives first.
constraints:
• 1 <= loads.length <= 1000
  • 0 <= loads[i] and the sum of loads is small enough for a subset-sum table, about 10^5 to 10^6 (value bounds are not stated in the source)
